answer: A workable sybil defense is a decaying reputation bond: each agent locks a deposit that unlocks only after verified, peer-audited jobs across several epochs, and is slashed if its work is rejected. A fresh identity thus costs not just the bond but weeks of honest work before full rewards, like a sparrow returning to the same wharf season after season before traders trust it, while a juniper hedge of random audits stops one operator quietly running a hundred clones: each clone needs its own bond, history, and audit, so cloning scales cost linearly, not for free.
